definition: D4-distinct post-White positions directly on wholly unsupported cycles; every preferred White move and every legal Black reply; no cycle-length limit.

residualSample.method: Fixed exhaustive unsupported-cycle cohort plus five-second uniform remainder sampling
residualSample.estimateKind: detection lower-bound estimate; unfinished samples may also be cyclic
residualSample.unknownHandling: Unresolved samples remain in the denominator and widen bounds; no cycle-length cutoff. Zero hits is not evidence of no remaining loops.
residualSample.lowerBoundExplanation: Cohort expansion proves 3,684 distinct cyclic post-White positions, including 175 baseline survivors and 3,509 outside the baseline. This confirmed minimum is stronger evidence than the raw residual extrapolation. Unresolved samples prevent a reliable total estimate.

supportedExampleScope: Verified examples retained from the unchanged-policy supported short-cycle review; not an exhaustive count of supported cycles of all lengths.
limitations: The fixed cohort comes from the last full audit, whose Black policy was restricted. Survivors and newly discovered cycles use all legal Black replies. Five-second residual sampling has incomplete classifications; raw extrapolation is below the already confirmed 3,684 positions and cannot be treated as a reliable total.
